workspace.trellis:title: Good Rubric Design
workspace.trellis:description: A rubric ontology that makes grading legible: distinct criteria, described performance levels, calibrated weighting, and feedback baked into the structure.

rubric-schema.description: A rubric that makes the same work score roughly the same no matter who's holding the pen — usable before and after the work is done.

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: What 'good' looks like at a glance — the sanity-check paragraph for someone who didn't design the assignment

fields.name: calibrated
fields.description: Have two graders scored the same sample work and landed within acceptable range?

fields.name: calibrationNotes
fields.description: What changed after calibration — where descriptions were too vague or subjective

fields.name: criteria
fields.description: Distinct, non-overlapping criteria — each measures something the others don't

fields.name: totalPoints
fields.description: Point allocation should mirror real priorities of the task

criterion-schema.description: One row of the rubric — measures a distinct quality with described performance levels.

fields.name: measures
fields.description: What this criterion alone evaluates — must not overlap with sibling criteria

fields.name: distinctFrom
fields.description: Explicit note on what this criterion does NOT score (prevents double-penalizing)

fields.name: maxPoints
fields.description: Weight within the rubric — should reflect how much this quality matters for the assignment

fields.name: levels
fields.description: Described performance levels — not just Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor labels

performance-level-schema.description: An observable description of work at a given level — the score comes with a reason attached.

fields.name: points
fields.description: Points awarded at this level for this criterion

fields.name: observableDescription
fields.description: What work at this level looks like in concrete, observable terms — not 'shows strong understanding'

fields.name: feedbackPrompt
fields.description: Suggested annotation language when circling this level — bakes feedback into the structure

nodes.trellis:title: Ontology Prototype Rubric
nodes.trellis:description: Grades the studio project where students design a domain ontology
nodes.purpose: Good work defines distinct entity types with non-overlapping fields, at least one relation with explicit cardinality, and one computed field whose formula is inspectable. It should be readable by someone who didn't design the domain.
nodes.calibrationNotes: Initial 'Design Quality' criterion overlapped with 'Clarity' — split into 'Schema Distinctness' vs 'Documentation Clarity'. Two sample prototypes rescored; graders now within 5 points.

nodes.trellis:title: Schema Distinctness
nodes.measures: Whether each entity type and field measures something the others don't — no double-penalizing the same flaw.
nodes.distinctFrom: Does NOT evaluate prose quality, completeness of sample data, or implementation correctness.

nodes.trellis:title: Relations & Structure
nodes.measures: Explicit relations with cardinality, synced properties where appropriate, and sequencing logic that a reader can follow.
nodes.distinctFrom: Does NOT evaluate naming aesthetics or number of entity types — a small, coherent ontology beats a sprawling one.

nodes.trellis:title: Checkability
nodes.measures: Fields and objectives that allow verifying progress without relying on vibes — checkbox fields, verification methods, observable descriptions.
nodes.distinctFrom: Does NOT evaluate visual design of projections or code quality.

nodes.trellis:title: Documentation Clarity
nodes.measures: Field descriptions that let someone plan work before doing it — readable as a reference, not just legible in hindsight.
nodes.distinctFrom: Does NOT evaluate schema correctness or relation wiring — those are Schema Distinctness and Relations.

nodes.trellis:title: Distinctness — Exemplary
nodes.label: exemplary
nodes.observableDescription: Every entity type has a one-sentence 'measures' statement; no two fields score the same quality; distinctFrom notes on overlapping criteria.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Schema types are cleanly separated — each field earns its place.

nodes.trellis:title: Distinctness — Proficient
nodes.label: proficient
nodes.observableDescription: Types are mostly distinct; one or two fields could merge without losing information.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Solid separation — consider merging [X] and [Y] which both track similar qualities.

nodes.trellis:title: Distinctness — Developing
nodes.label: developing
nodes.observableDescription: Multiple fields or types overlap in practice; a grader would double-count the same flaw or strength.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Overlap between [fields/types] — define what each one alone measures.

nodes.trellis:title: Distinctness — Beginning
nodes.label: beginning
nodes.observableDescription: Generic field names (notes, description, status) with no distinct measurement role.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Fields need sharper roles — what does each one alone evaluate?

nodes.trellis:title: Relations — Exemplary
nodes.label: exemplary
nodes.observableDescription: At least two relations with explicit cardinality and syncedProperty; buildsOn or equivalent makes sequencing logic readable.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Relations carry the structure — sequencing is explicit.

nodes.trellis:title: Relations — Proficient
nodes.label: proficient
nodes.observableDescription: Relations present with cardinality; sequencing implied but not fully documented.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Good relation wiring — make the 'why this order' logic explicit in module or buildsOn fields.

nodes.trellis:title: Checkability — Exemplary
nodes.label: exemplary
nodes.observableDescription: Major outcomes have checkable flags, verification methods, or observable level descriptions — grader and student can agree on progress.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Objectives and key fields are verifiable — not vibe-based.

nodes.trellis:title: Checkability — Developing
nodes.label: developing
nodes.observableDescription: Outcomes use vague language ('understand', 'demonstrate knowledge') without verification path.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Replace vague outcomes with observable verbs and a verification method.

nodes.trellis:title: Documentation — Exemplary
nodes.label: exemplary
nodes.observableDescription: A reader who didn't design the assignment can describe what good work looks like from field descriptions alone.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Descriptions work as a planning guide — usable before submission.

nodes.trellis:title: Documentation — Beginning
nodes.label: beginning
nodes.observableDescription: Descriptions empty or generic; rubric/ontology only makes sense after seeing an example.
nodes.feedbackPrompt: Descriptions function as excuse generators — rewrite for someone planning work, not grading it.

calibrated-rubrics.description: Rubrics that passed the two-grader calibration test
calibrated-rubrics.eqls: FIND root AS ?r WHERE ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.@type = 'Rubric' AND ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.calibrated = true RETURN ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.assignmentTitle

criteria-with-distinctFrom.eqls: FIND root AS ?r WHERE ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.@type = 'Criterion' AND ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.distinctFrom != null RETURN ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.name, ?r.workspace.graph.nodes.distinctFrom
